findings.summary: getChildContext provides reactIconBase via legacy context API, but react-icons v5.5.0 Md* icons (MdMoreVert) use modern React.createContext(IconContext) exclusively and do not read from childContextTypes; the color '#8e8e8e' customization for the more-menu button icon is lost, and the icon reverts to inherited currentColor (white#f0f0f0 on black header background#191b20)
findings.failure_scenario: Render the LayerEditor component. The MdMoreVert icon in the header more-menu button renders with fill=currentColor (inherits #f0f0f0 white from html element) instead of the intended #8e8e8e gray, because react-icons v5.5.0 ignores the reactIconBase legacy context and CSS rules for .more-menu__button__svg set only width/height (24px) without setting fill/color.

findings.summary: Error dismiss link uses href='#' without event.preventDefault(), causing the browser to navigate to # and scroll to page top when the user clicks 'x' to dismiss the duplicate-ID error
findings.failure_scenario: User triggers a duplicate layer ID error, sees the error message with an 'x' dismiss button. Clicking the 'x' (<a href='#' onClick={() => this.setState({ error: null })}>) clears the error state but also navigates the browser to href='#', scrolling the page to the top. The arrow function does not receive the event parameter, so no preventDefault() is possible.
